chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: When it was the year forty-one, Muawiya intended to perform Hajj, so he sent a carpenter and sent the tools, and wrote to the governor of Medina that he should remove the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and make it according to the measure of his own pulpit in Syria. So when they rose to remove it, the sun was eclipsed and the earth was shaken, so they refrained and wrote about that to Muawiya. So he wrote back to them, stressing upon them to do what they were doing. So they did that, and the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is the entrance which you see.

key_terms.مِنْبَرُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Pulpit of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What happened to the Prophet's pulpit in Medina during Muawiya's time?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the political and spiritual tension between the Umayyad caliphate and the Ahl al-Bayt, as Muawiya’s removal of the Prophet’s pulpit—a symbol of prophetic authority—was met with celestial signs of divine displeasure. The event underscores the Shia scholarly view that the physical relocation of sacred artifacts often coincides with a shift in religious legitimacy, while the subsequent earthquake and eclipse serve as cosmic affirmations of the Prophet’s enduring presence in Medina.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When it was the year forty one, Muawiya intended the Hajj. So he sent carpenters and sent the tools, and wrote to the governor of Al-Medina that he should get rid of the Pulpit of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> and make it to be upon a measurement of his own pulpit which was in Syria.  So, when they got ready to get rid of it, the sun eclipsed and the ground shook.  So, they refrained and wrote about that to Muawiya. So he wrote back to them, stressing upon them to what they should be doing. So they did that, and the Pulpit of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> is (today) the entrance which one can see’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘In the year forty-one Mu‘awiyah decided to perform al-Hajj. He sent certain carpenters with tools with orders to the governor of al-Madinah to remove the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and position it in place of his pulpit in Damascus. When they began to remove the pulpit, a sun eclipse took place and the earth began to shake. They stopped the work and wrote about it to Mu‘awiyah. He wrote back and urged them to do what they were ordered to do before. They then complied with the order and today the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah is the opening that you can see.”
